facts.fact: UNDP's report on 2024 says that for decades proving identity in Guinea-Bissau depended on paper records handwritten in old registers, and that this was beginning to change with a process to digitise the registers; the only digital work it reports for 2024 is that back-digitisation, not entry at registration.

systems.system: Digitisation of civil registry books (Legal ID for All)
systems.owner: Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, with UNDP; funded by the Swiss Confederation
systems.tiers: more than 7,500 registry books and 1.3 million civil acts catalogued in five regions; in Bissau all civil birth registry books digitised, 230,967 records; headline figure of 1.7 million civil and identity records digitised
launched 2021; scaled to national coverage in 2024, eastern, southern, northern and island regions; 3,288 children registered in a 15-day deployment

systems.system: Interoperability of the civil registration database with national identity card, voter registration, social protection and judiciary
National Statistical Report on Civil Registration (2018-2022)
systems.owner: Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, Ministry of Public Health, INE, UNDP, UNICEF
systems.tiers: first national vital statistics report from civil registration, published in 2024

note: SIREC is not named in this report; the digital work reported for 2024 is archive digitisation and a mobile campaign.
